title: Google DeepMind unveils a senior-researcher retention package by Q4 2026
body: The same-week exits of Nobel laureate John Jumper to Anthropic and Gemini co-lead Noam Shazeer to OpenAI mark an acceleration of senior research talent leaving Google, and the financial backdrop shows why poaching is affordable for rivals: OpenAI tripled revenue year over year to 5.7 billion dollars in the first quarter and sits on more than 73 billion dollars in cash after its spring raise, ammunition that funds aggressive compensation. Google already paid a reported 2.7 billion dollars under two years ago to bring Shazeer's team back, so losing him plus a marquee AlphaFold name in a 48-hour window is the kind of reputational and capability loss that forces a structural response rather than one-off counteroffers. Expect Google or DeepMind leadership to roll out a named retention and compensation mechanism aimed at its most senior researchers ahead of the next Gemini cycle, whether framed as accelerated equity, multi-year founder-style grants, or expanded autonomy and compute guarantees for principal scientists.

reasoning.because: Jumper and Shazeer both exited Google in one 48-hour window for Anthropic and OpenAI respectively
reasoning.given: Cash-rich rivals can outbid, and Google already paid 2.7B to retain Shazeer once
reasoning.so_that: Google moves from ad hoc counteroffers to a structural senior-researcher retention program before its next Gemini launch
reasoning.landing: Google or DeepMind announces a named retention package by Q4 2026
reasoning.plain_language: Google's star AI scientists keep leaving for rivals, so Google will likely offer a big new deal to keep the rest.

summary: John Jumper left Google DeepMind for Anthropic and Gemini co-lead Noam Shazeer left for OpenAI in one 48-hour window, leaving Google with a senior-talent exodus as cash-rich rivals outbid it. Expect Google or DeepMind to announce a structural retention package for senior researchers by Q4 2026.
